prize_parts.citation: for showing how firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment shape international trade, aggregate productivity and the gains from openness

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged: one part, B020, credited to Melitz and Helpman. Round 1 did not change my view of the science. It did sharpen my wording and my confidence. I weight three common criteria: how much the contribution changed what is known and measured, how well it has held up under replication and extension, and how cleanly credit can be assigned. On the first two B020 is strongest among the four leading candidates. Moving the unit of analysis from industry to firm changed how trade data are collected, estimated and used in policy evaluation. The core mechanisms are selection into exporting, reallocation toward more productive firms, and the exporting-versus-FDI margin. These have been confronted with firm-level data across many countries for over two decades. On the third criterion B020 is weaker than B001. I regard that as a real cost, not a technicality. It is a cost I accept, because I judge the size and verifiability of the change in knowledge to matter more than tidiness of credit. The citation I propose names the mechanism (firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment) and does not claim to credit the firm-level empirical literature as a whole.
statement.case_against: The credit boundary is the main weakness. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum supplied firm-level facts and closely related models and are not on the credited list. Within the three-name cap I cannot repair that. A Melitz-Helpman award would be contestable on priority in a way a Grossman-Helpman award would not. Second, some gains-from-trade magnitudes depend on parametric assumptions, such as Pareto productivity and CES demand. The qualitative mechanism is better supported than the quantitative welfare claims. Third, Helpman is credited on B001, and the committee must pick one body of his work to honour. I also concede that my earlier contrast was too sharp. Mixed tests of protection-for-sale and parametric dependence in B020 welfare numbers are both cases of contested magnitudes. The difference between B020 and B001 is real but narrower than my first-round wording suggested. Finally, B020 and B001 are both trade awards after 2008, so the field-balance argument does not separate them.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B001 first. She argues that mixed results in testing a model with sharp predictions are normal, not evidence of failure, and asks the committee to separate contested magnitudes from no lasting contribution. She also says that B020 has an unsettled attribution (Redding, and Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum) with no comparable gap in B001.
responses.response: I accept the distinction between contested magnitudes and no lasting contribution, and I withdraw any implication that B001 is a framework without lasting impact. It gave empiricists a structural equation to estimate and shaped how the field poses the question. Where we still differ is weighting. Under my criteria the larger change in what economists measure and routinely do with data counts for more than cleaner credit. You are right that the B020 gap has no counterpart in B001. I treat it as a risk that is bounded by wording the citation around the mechanism, not as something that makes B001 the better science. I regard the choice as close, and B001 is my first alternative.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B001 first and B020 as his first alternative. He regards the B020 attribution gap as the main reason to rank it lower and does not want B001 to rest on credit earned from Helpman's other work. He asks for a clear argument for why Melitz and Helpman, rather than a wider group, define the contribution.
responses.response: I agree that B001 must stand on protection for sale and the trade-innovation-growth models alone, and I do not use Helpman's B020 work to argue against it. My answer to your request is as follows. The contribution I would credit is the conceptual model of selection (Melitz 2003) and its extension to the exporting-versus-FDI choice (Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple 2004). Both are identifiable in these two names. The empirical firm-level facts and closely related models by Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are precursors and parallel work whose omission I should say plainly, and I would want the Scientific Background to describe them fully. Whether that is enough to avoid a priority dispute is your point, and I cannot dismiss it. It is the reason B001 is my first alternative and not a distant one.

responses.point: Hassler, who prefers B016, says the B020 argument carries real weight and that he did not rank B020 in his opening. He asks that B020 be stated directly against B001, since Helpman is a bridge between them. He also asks that the choice be made on the strength of each contribution and not on the overlap.
responses.response: Taking your request directly, I set B020 against B001 on the three criteria above. On change in what is known and measured, B020 is stronger, because it altered data use, estimation and quantitative evaluation of trade policy, while the influence of B001 is mainly through theory. On durability, both are mature, and B020 has been checked against firm-level data more widely. On clean credit, B001 is clearly stronger. I do not think Helpman's presence in both should favour either, and I do not count him as a bridge. The committee has to choose a strand. On B016, I read your point about breadth and the 2024 overlap as serious, and I do not rank it because I find the evidential side of B020 more directly checkable. That is a difference of weighting. I do not regard it as a verdict on B016's quality.

responses.point: Strömberg ranks B020 first and argues that, because the missing names are not on the credited list, the committee should handle the boundary in the citation wording. He regards a third seat for Redding as arguable but prefers the narrower award, and he names B031 and B001 as alternatives.
responses.response: I agree with the wording approach and have adopted it in the citation. I also agree that I cannot responsibly add uncredited names. On Redding, I stay with two names. His quantitative and spatial work builds on the established framework. A third seat would credit extension and not the originating step, and it would add a further apportionment question to a case that already has one. I note your remark that B031 is a strong alternative. I rank it lower than B001 for the 2022-overlap reason you raise, so I keep B001 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Andersson, a Lund colleague, ranks B001 first for its clean pair attribution and durable influence beyond trade. He ranks B020 as a serious alternative but would want the credit boundary settled before putting it above B001. He raises an unverified question about how much of B001's novelty lies in the application of earlier common-agency machinery.
responses.response: I take your condition seriously, and I cannot settle the boundary by adding names. I can only say that I judge the Melitz-Helpman core defensible and that the boundary is a risk the committee should weigh openly. Your unverified question about common-agency machinery is also one I cannot resolve, and I have not verified it myself. If it holds, it narrows the novelty gap between B001 and B020 and strengthens your point that mixed empirical tests do not undercut the framework's contribution. I do not offer it as an argument against you. It is a reason I would not be dismayed by a B001 outcome.

uncertainties: Whether omitting Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum is disqualifying or can be handled in citation wording and the Scientific Background. I lean toward the latter, with moderate confidence.

If the committee recognises trade, I would accept B001 as a single-part award. B001 is my clear second choice, and I regard Helpman's role in both strands as a reason to choose between them, not to combine them.
How far the B020 welfare-gains magnitudes depend on parametric assumptions, and whether the case then rests more on the selection and reallocation mechanisms than on quantitative results.

Whether the committee will apply one common weighting of identification quality, framework breadth and cumulative field-building to B001, B016, B019 and B020. My own weighting favours change in measurement and checkability, and other members weight clean credit and breadth more.
My knowledge of priority claims comes from memory and the round-1 files, and I have not independently verified it.
statement.conflict_note: No tie to Helpman, Melitz or any other credited name on B020, B001 or B014 is apparent from my supplied profile. For disclosure: Tommy Andersson is a Lund colleague and prefers B001. Jan Teorell was formerly at Lund, and the profile records no link to any candidate. My Lund economic-history co-authors are not credited on any shortlisted ballot ID. These are disclosed and not adjudicated. Round 1 did not reveal any new connection of mine.
